exercises.name: Power Snatch

source_english.description: A power snatch pulls a barbell from the floor to an overhead catch in one explosive movement.
instructions: Set the bar over the mid-foot and take a wide overhand grip with a flat back.
Lift the bar close to the legs and extend the hips and knees powerfully.
Pull under the bar and receive it overhead in a partial squat with locked arms.
Stand tall, then lower the bar to the floor under control.
form_cues: Finish the extension before pulling under.
common_mistakes: Catching with soft or uneven elbows.
source_english.safety_note: Use a light load, clear the area, and stop if the overhead catch is unstable.

source_english.description: Running uses a repeating stride with relaxed posture, soft foot contact, and a steady forward or in-place rhythm.
instructions: Start by standing upright with your feet hip-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your upper body relaxed.
Begin jogging in place, lifting your knees up towards your chest and landing softly on the balls of your feet.
Maintain a steady pace and continue jogging for the desired duration or distance.
Remember to breathe deeply and maintain good posture throughout the exercise.
source_english.safety_note: Choose a pace and surface that allow controlled breathing and stable landings.

source_english.description: Skating uses repeated side-to-side bounds with one-foot landings and the free leg sweeping behind the body.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and bend the knees slightly.
Bound to the right and land softly on the right foot.
Swing the left leg behind the right and tap the floor, then bound to the left.
Alternate sides while keeping the landings quiet and controlled.
form_cues: Keep the chest angled slightly forward.
Push sideways through the whole foot.
source_english.safety_note: Use a non-slip surface and reduce the distance if single-leg landings become unstable.

exercises.name: Sprints

source_english.description: Sprints are short, fast running efforts separated by walking or standing recovery.
instructions: Choose a measured straight path and begin with an easy warm-up pace.
Accelerate with a forward lean, driving the knees and arms in opposition.
Run hard for the planned distance or time while keeping the stride controlled.
Decelerate gradually, recover, and repeat only after breathing settles.
form_cues: Keep the foot strike under the hips.
Drive the arms straight ahead and back.
common_mistakes: Starting at maximum speed without a warm-up.
source_english.safety_note: Use a clear, level surface and stop if stride mechanics or balance deteriorate.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry (Dumbbell)

source_english.description: A dumbbell suitcase carry walks while one heavy dumbbell hangs at one side, challenging the trunk to resist leaning.
instructions: Stand tall with one dumbbell at your side and the other arm relaxed.
Brace the abdomen and keep the shoulders and hips level.
Walk forward with short, controlled steps while keeping the dumbbell from touching the thigh.
Stop at the planned distance, set the weight down safely, and switch sides.
common_mistakes: Leaning toward or away from the dumbbell.
Turning before the weight is controlled.
source_english.safety_note: Use a clear walking lane and a weight you can set down without dropping.
